title: ÆTHER album Kaattu Thee, song 4: Dance (instrumental, 90 s, one take)
story: Rudra's friends drag him into the street wedding procession and the whole lane turns into a dance floor.

brief.notes: Jithesh 13:35: 'Now dance.' Instrumental like the locked intro. One take only (his rule 13:29). He called the 60 s fight tests 'incomplete versions', so this is 90 s with a full shape: intro, hook, second section, a breakdown, the biggest hook, and a real ending. Indian touch = Tamil film writing style (bounce, tisram switch, stop-and-slam hits, hook returning bigger), not only Indian instruments.

prompt: A complete, high-energy modern Tamil film dance number, instrumental, new-generation Kollywood style for a street wedding procession. ONE irresistible, bouncy, catchy hook melody in a bright minor key with an Indian flavour, played on a reedy nadaswaram-like synth lead with playful bends and slides, answered by a whistle and punchy brass. Swinging dappankuthu bounce at 110 BPM: loud thappu and parai drums with a tight kick, snappy claps, deep 808 bass and modern EDM synth stabs, a gang 'hey' shout on the big beats. Clean, wide, musical production with space, not noisy. Full song shape: an 8 second drum roll intro, the hook, a second melody section with a veena and synth call-and-answer, a switch into a fast triplet tisram groove, a short stop of silence and a crowd shout, a breakdown with only drums and claps building faster, then the biggest final hook with everyone playing, and a proper ending: a fast drum korvai and one last full-band hit.
